tools.description:
Execute a `bash` command. Use this for shell semantics — pipes, env, processes, git, package managers, build/test runners, anything genuinely interactive or multi-step.

**Translate these to a dedicated tool instead:**
- `cat` / `head` / `tail` (known path) → `Read`
- `sed` / `awk` (in-place edit) → `Edit`
- `echo > file` / `cat <<EOF` → `Write`
- `find` / recursive `ls` to locate files by name pattern → `Glob` (plain `ls <known-directory>` is fine for listing a directory)
- `grep` / `rg` (search file contents) → `Grep`
- `echo` / `printf` (talk to the user) → just output text directly

The dedicated tools render in the per-tool permission UI and keep raw stdout out of the conversation; that is why they are worth reaching for whenever one fits.

**Output:**
The stdout and stderr will be combined and returned as a string. The output may be truncated if it is too long. If the command exits non-zero, the output ends with a `Command failed with exit code: N` line; a command killed by its timeout or interrupted by the user ends with its own message instead.

Background execution is disabled for this agent. Do not set `run_in_background=true`.

**Guidelines for safety and security:**
- Each shell tool call will be executed in a fresh shell environment. The shell variables, current working directory changes, and the shell history is not preserved between calls. To run a command in a particular directory, pass the `cwd` argument (or use absolute paths) rather than relying on a `cd` from an earlier call.
- The tool call will return after the command is finished. You shall not use this tool to execute an interactive command or a command that may run forever. For possibly long-running commands, set the `timeout` argument in seconds. The default is 60s; foreground commands allow up to 300s; a foreground command that hits its timeout is killed.
- Avoid using `..` to access files or directories outside of the working directory.
- Avoid modifying files outside of the working directory unless explicitly instructed to do so.
- Never run commands that require superuser privileges unless explicitly instructed to do so.

**Guidelines for efficiency:**
- Use `&&` to chain commands that genuinely depend on each other, e.g. `npm install && npm test`. Independent read-only commands (separate `git show`, `ls`, or status checks) should be issued as separate parallel Bash calls in one response, not chained into a single call — chaining serializes their execution and mixes their output. Do not stitch outputs together with `echo` separators.
- Use `;` to run commands sequentially regardless of success/failure
- Use `||` for conditional execution (run second command only if first fails)
- Use pipe operations (`|`) and redirections (`>`, `>>`) to chain input and output between commands
- Always quote file paths containing spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "/path with spaces/")
- Compose multi-step logic in a single call with `if` / `case` / `for` / `while` control flows.
- Do not set `run_in_background=true`; background task management tools are not available.

**Commands available:**
The following common command categories are usually available. Availability still depends on the host, so when in doubt run `which <command>` first to confirm a command exists before relying on it.
- Navigation and inspection: `ls`, `pwd`, `cd`, `stat`, `file`, `du`, `df`, `tree`
- File and directory management: `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `ln`, `chmod`, `chown`
- Text and data processing: `wc`, `sort`, `uniq`, `cut`, `tr`, `diff`, `xargs`
- Archives and compression: `tar`, `gzip`, `gunzip`, `zip`, `unzip`
- Networking and transfer: `curl`, `wget`, `ping`, `ssh`, `scp`
- Version control: `git`; for GitHub-hosted work (PRs, issues, CI runs, API queries) prefer the `gh` CLI when installed — it carries the user's GitHub auth and can return structured JSON
- Process and system: `ps`, `kill`, `top`, `env`, `date`, `uname`, `whoami`
- Language and package toolchains: `node`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `python`, `pip` (use whichever the project actually relies on)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

3	Rich-Go will enrich `go test` outputs with text decorations.
4	
5	[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/99810.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/99810)
6	
7	## Description
8	
9	richgo is a command-line tool that adds color and formatting to the output of Go's `go test` command, making test results easier to read and understand.
10	
11	## Installation
12	
13	### Using go get
14	
15	```
16	go get -u github.com/kyoh86/richgo
17	```
18

32	## Usage
33	
34	### Basic Usage
35	
36	```sh
37	richgo test ./...
38	```
39	
40	### In an existing pipeline
41	
42	If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.

61	```

65	### Configuration file paths

69	* `${CWD}/.richstyle`

164	
165	### Line categories
166	
167	Rich-Go separates the output lines into the following categories:
168	
169	* **Build**: Build error messages
170	* **Start**: Test start lines (e.g., `=== RUN   TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
171	* **Pass**: Test pass lines (e.g., `--- PASS: TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
172	* **Fail**: Test failure lines (e.g., `--- FAIL: TestSampleNG (0.00s)`)
173	* **Skip**: Test skip lines (e.g., `--- SKIP: TestSampleSkip (0.00s)`)
174	* **PassPackage**: Package pass indicator (`PASS`)
175	* **FailPackage**: Package fail indicator (`FAIL`)
176	* **Cover**: Coverage analysis lines
177	
178	Each category can be styled separately.
179	
180	### Label types
181	
182	* **Long**: BUILD, START, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, COVER
183	* **Short**: !!, >, o, x, -, %
184	* **None**: Rich-Go will never output labels.

192	  foreground: yellow

196	  foreground: green

# DOMAIN 4 — Style attributes & color syntax (richgo `testfilter`)

All runs used `RICHGO_LOCAL=1 RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` in a `mktemp -d` CWD with a `.richstyle` file; input piped via stdin. Reference input line: `--- PASS: TestFoo (0.00s)\n`, which renders (default) as `ESC[32mPASS | Foo (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`.

## 1. Rendering pipeline per styled line

`<bg-seq?><fg-seq?><attr-seqs...>TEXTESC[0m\n`

- Each component is a SEPARATE escape sequence, emitted in this fixed order:
  1. **background** color (if set)
  2. **foreground** color (if set)
  3. **attributes** in fixed numeric order (regardless of YAML key order)
- Then the decorated text, then a single `ESC[0m` immediately **before** the `\n`.
- If a style is completely empty (no colors, no attrs — e.g. `foreground: ""` with nothing else), NO escapes are emitted at all, not even `ESC[0m`: output is plain `PASS | Foo (0.00s)\n`.
- Config **merges** with built-in defaults field-by-field: setting only `passStyle.bold: true` keeps default green fg → `ESC[32mESC[1m...`. Setting `buildStyle.bold: false` removes the default bold → only `ESC[33m`. `null` values = unset (default kept).

## 2. Boolean attributes (exact codes)

| YAML key | sequence |
|---|---|
| `bold` | `ESC[1m` |
| `faint` | `ESC[2m` |
| `italic` | `ESC[3m` |
| `underline` | `ESC[4m` |
| `blinkSlow` | `ESC[5m` |
| `blinkRapid` | `ESC[6m` |
| `inverse` | `ESC[7m` |
| `conceal` | `ESC[8m` |
| `crossOut` | `ESC[9m` |
| `frame` | `ESC[51m` |
| `encircle` | `ESC[52m` |
| `overline` | `ESC[53m` |

All 13 set at once (YAML in scrambled order) emitted, verbatim:
`ESC[32m ESC[1m ESC[2m ESC[3m ESC[4m ESC[5m ESC[6m ESC[7m ESC[8m ESC[9m ESC[51m ESC[52m ESC[53m PASS | Foo (0.00s) ESC[0m \n`
(fg first because no bg was set). Full combo `background: red, foreground: blue, bold+underline`:
`ESC[41m ESC[34m ESC[1m ESC[4m PASS | Foo (0.00s) ESC[0m \n`

YAML typing: `bold: yes` works (YAML bool); `bold: 1` or `bold: "true"` → whole-file config error (see §6). Unknown keys (e.g. `sparkle: true`) are silently ignored.

## 3. Named colors (case-sensitive; only these exact spellings)

| name | fg | bg |
|---|---|---|
| `black` | 30 | 40 |
| `red` | 31 | 41 |
| `green` | 32 | 42 |
| `yellow` | 33 | 43 |
| `blue` | 34 | 44 |
| `magenta` | 35 | 45 |
| `cyan` | 36 | 46 |
| `white` | 37 | 47 |
| `lightBlack` | 90 | 100 |
| `lightRed` | 91 | 101 |
| `lightGreen` | 92 | 102 |
| `lightYellow` | 93 | 103 |
| `lightBlue` | 94 | 104 |
| `lightMagenta` | 95 | 105 |
| `lightCyan` | 96 | 106 |
| `lightWhite` | 97 | 107 |

- Special name **`default`** = "no color": accepted, emits nothing, and *removes* the inherited default color (`passStyle: {foreground: default, bold: true}` → `ESC[1m...ESC[0m`, no color seq).
- REJECTED (config error, §6): `gray`, `grey`, `lightGray`, `lightGrey`, `darkGray`, `darkGrey`, `Red`, `RED`, `Green`, `LightBlack`, `lightblack`, `White`, `normal`, `orange`, `pink`, `brown`, `purple`, `silver`, `navy`, `teal`, `lime`, `aqua`, `fuchsia`, `maroon`, `olive`, `lightPink`, `darkRed`, `brightRed`, `brightBlack`, `light`, `Light`.

## 4. Hex and rgb() colors

- **`#rrggbb`** (exactly 6 hex digits, `#` required; upper/lower/mixed case OK): fg → `ESC[38;2;R;G;Bm`, bg → `ESC[48;2;R;G;Bm` (decimal components).
  - `#ff0000`/`#FF0000` → `ESC[38;2;255;0;0m`; `#a1B2c3` → `ESC[38;2;161;178;195m`; bg `#00ff10` → `ESC[48;2;0;255;16m`.
  - REJECTED: `#rgb` (`#f00`, `#F00`), `#12345`, `#1234567`, missing `#` (`ff0000`), bad digits (`#gg0000`), `#12`, `#`.
- **`rgb(r,g,b)`** — prefix `rgb` is case-INSENSITIVE (`RGB`, `RgB`, `rGb` all work):
  - Decimal: `rgb(255,0,0)` → `ESC[38;2;255;0;0m`; leading zeros OK (`rgb(001,002,003)` → `1;2;3`); range 0–255 (`rgb(256,0,0)`, `rgb(0377,0,0)`, `rgb(-1,0,0)` rejected).
  - Hex components: `rgb(0xff,0x00,0x00)` → `255;0;0`; `0x`/`0X` OK; **exactly 2 hex digits required** (`rgb(0x01,0x02,0x03)` → `1;2;3`, but `rgb(0x1,0x2,0x3)` and `rgb(0x100,0,0)` rejected).
  - Whitespace: spaces allowed only AFTER commas (`rgb(255, 0, 0)` OK); space after `(`, before `)`, or before a comma (`rgb( 255,...)`, `rgb(255 ,0,0)`, `rgb(255,0,0 )`) rejected. Exactly 3 components required.
- **Integer / 256-palette**: YAML int or quoted numeric string 0–255 → `ESC[38;5;Nm` fg / `ESC[48;5;Nm` bg. Verified 0,7,8,15,16,200,255 OK (both `123` and `"123"`); 256, -1, 1000 → config error.
- Empty string `""` = valid, means no color (like `default`).

## 5. `hide: true` semantics per category

- `hide: true` drops the line's output entirely (nothing, not even newline). Verified for `startStyle`, `passStyle`, `failStyle`, `skipStyle`, `buildStyle` (hides BOTH the `# pkg` header line and the following message lines), `coveredStyle`/`uncoveredStyle` (standalone `coverage: X% of statements` lines), and `passPackageStyle`/`failPackageStyle` (default config already hides both).
- `hide: false` explicitly re-enables: `passPackageStyle: {hide: false}` on input `PASS\n` → `ESC[32mPASSESC[0m\n` (raw text, no label prefix). `failPackageStyle: {hide: false}` on `FAIL\n` → `ESC[31mESC[1mFAILESC[0m\n`.
- `fileStyle.hide: true` / `lineStyle.hide: true` don't drop the line; they drop just the filename / `:N:N` segments inside build-error lines (see §7), leaving the rest.
- Note: `ok  \tpkg\t0.1s\tcoverage: 80.0% of statements` lines are NOT affected by covered/uncovered styles at all (they take passPackage green without hiding) — coverage styling only applies to standalone `coverage:` lines.

## 6. Invalid color / config error behavior

- Any invalid color (bad name, bad hex, bad rgb(), out-of-range int) or YAML type error causes the **entire config file to be discarded** — all other valid customizations in the same file are lost and built-in defaults apply. Loading continues with the NEXT file in the search order (verified: bad `.richstyle` + valid `.richstyle.yaml` → the `.yaml` was still applied).
- Error goes to **stderr** via Go `log` (timestamp prefix), exit code stays **0**, processing continues. Exact bytes (one line):
  `2026/08/08 11:23:23 error unmarshaling yaml from /tmp/.../.richstyle :  invalid format\n`
  (note the doubled space: `<path> :␣␣invalid format` — pattern is `... : ` + error text, and the color error text itself is ` invalid format` with a leading space, or equivalent).
- YAML structural/type errors surface the yaml library message after the same prefix, e.g.:
  - `... :  yaml: unmarshal errors:\n  line 2: cannot unmarshal !!int `1` into bool` (multi-line, literal newlines in the log output)
  - `... :  yaml: line 1: did not find expected ',' or ']'`

## 7. Reset (`ESC[0m`) behavior + the BUILD-line quirk

- Normal styled lines: `ESC[0m` immediately before `\n`.
- **`# pkg` build-header lines: reset comes AFTER the newline** — input `# example/pkg\n` outputs exactly:
  `ESC[33m ESC[1m BUILD| example/pkg \n ESC[0m`
  i.e. the `ESC[0m` dangles at the start of the next line (or at EOF — output ends with `\nESC[0m`, no trailing newline after it; a `\n` is even added if the input lacked one). Every `#`-prefixed line reopens the style (`# a\n# b\n` → two full `BUILD|` blocks each with reset-after-`\n`).
- Build-error message lines (`./main.go:10:2: undefined: foo`) render with a blank label of the same width as `BUILD|` (6 spaces incl. `|`) and nest file/line styles, e.g.:
  `ESC[33m ESC[1m "     | " ESC[36m ./main.go ESC[0m ESC[35m :10:2 ESC[0m ESC[33m ESC[1m : undefined: foo ESC[0m \n`
  — fileStyle span (`./main.go`), reset, lineStyle span (`:10:2`), reset, then buildStyle **re-opened** for the remaining message text (`: undefined: foo`), reset, `\n`. The re-open after the file/line spans is unconditional (still emitted even when fileStyle/lineStyle are `hide: true`; hidden segments themselves emit nothing, not even their text).
- Extra classification note: any otherwise-unrecognized line that FOLLOWS a `# pkg` line is styled as a build-continuation line (blank label + buildStyle, normal reset-before-`\n`).
